title: Watercress Soup
subtitle: Vivid green watercress soup with a peppery kick
excerpt: Potato and onion base blended with fresh watercress to make a vivid, peppery green soup. One of Britain's oldest native greens in its most elegant form. Serve hot or chilled.

recipe.sourceNotes: Watercress is one of Britain's oldest cultivated greens, grown in chalk streams across Hampshire, Wiltshire, and Dorset since the 17th century. Watercress soup appeared in British recipe books by the 19th century and is particularly associated with the south of England. The potato base provides body and a creaminess that balances the peppery bite of the watercress. Like spinach soup, the colour fades quickly after blending: serve immediately or cool rapidly if making ahead.

recipeTools.notes: Plus a blender or stick blender.

content.text: Add the watercress only in the final minute of cooking, just long enough to wilt: longer cooking dulls both the colour and the distinctive peppery flavour. Blend immediately and serve straight away for the best colour. This soup is also very good chilled: cool quickly after blending and refrigerate.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the diced potato and stock. Bring to a boil and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until the potato is completely tender.
Add the watercress and stir to wilt for 1 minute. Remove from the heat immediately.
Blend until completely smooth. Stir in the cream. Season with salt and pepper. Serve immediately, or cool rapidly for a chilled soup.
